teamHeading: Meet the people behind One Life Advisory.
heroSub: We wanted financial planning to start with a person's life and the decisions they're trying to make. That means understanding what matters first, then figuring out how investments, income, insurance, taxes, and estate decisions fit together as life changes.
whyP1: We started One Life Advisory because we kept seeing the same gap. People with real responsibility and real resources, but with a financial life made up of pieces that didn't add up to a plan. Cash flow that wasn't coordinated with the investments. Investments that weren't coordinated with the protection. Protection hadn't been looked at in years. Decisions made by default instead of on purpose. And a vague sense of where it was all going, but no clear answer to the question that actually matters: is this money supporting the life I want to live, now and for every year ahead?
whyP2: We built One Life to close that gap. Planning, investments, protection, and the way taxes affect every move you make — all under one roof, all coordinated, all built around what you actually want out of this life.
closingSub: Start with a free Clarity Call. We'll spend 15 to 30 minutes getting to know your situation and seeing whether working together makes sense.

beliefs.title: A plan should start with purpose, not products.
beliefs.body: What you want your money to do is the foundation. Everything else is built on top of it. And every decision after that gets made on purpose, not by default or out of habit.

beliefs.title: Everything connects to everything.
beliefs.body: Cash flow affects investments. Investments affect taxes. Taxes affect what you can spend. Protection determines whether any of it survives the unexpected. We treat them as one plan because that's what they are.

beliefs.title: Money is a tool, not the goal.
beliefs.body: The goal is the life you want to live. The work we do is to make sure your money is good enough at its job that you can stop worrying about it and get on with the life.

differentP1:
We start by understanding what you want your money to do and what you are trying to accomplish.

Once we understand that, we can decide what investment changes, insurance, retirement income strategies, or other planning decisions may make sense. Each recommendation should connect back to something specific in the plan.
differentP2:
The emphasis will be different for every client. Some situations require more work around retirement income. Others need more attention around investments, protection, taxes, or estate planning.

Where we spend our time depends on what matters most in your situation.

team.name: Justin Gartman
team.bio:
Justin Gartman joined the firm because too many people arrive at retirement with a decent pile of savings and no real plan for what to do with it, and too many people on their way there make decisions now that end up costing them later.

He enjoys working with both groups - for people still building toward retirement, that means helping them make smarter moves along the way. The account choices, the tax decisions, the tradeoffs that are easy to miss but shape where they land years down the road. For people already at or near retirement, it means shifting the conversation from simply getting there to actually getting through it: turning savings into an income plan that holds up, adjusts to what life throws at it, and doesn't run out.

Justin loves educating clients along the way, not just handing them a recommendation. He'd rather spend the time walking through the why behind a decision, because clients who understand their plan are the ones who trust it and stick with it. That curiosity extends to the research side of retirement income planning too. He enjoys geeking out on many topics such as sequence-of-returns risk, how to build a genuine floor of guaranteed income, how different tools reinforce each other instead of working at odds. (he does it so you don't have to)

He lives in Coleman, Texas, with his wife and their four young kids.
